facts.text: A machine-learning detection network can learn renderer- or simulator-specific artefacts.
facts.quote: The network learns renderer- or simulator-specific artefacts.

facts.text: Simulated weather can fail to match real particle physics, with incorrect dust and fog optics.
facts.quote: Simulated weather does not match real particle physics; dust and fog optics, sensor noise, material reflectance and radar cross-section are wrong.

facts.text: Simulated sensor noise can be wrong in simulated or generated training data for machine-learning detection.
facts.quote: sensor noise, material reflectance and radar cross-section are wrong.

facts.text: Simulated material reflectance and radar cross-section can be wrong in simulated or generated training data for machine-learning detection.
facts.quote: material reflectance and radar cross-section are wrong.

facts.text: Object geometry can be unrealistically clean in simulated or generated training data for machine-learning detection.
Contamination and vibration can be missing from simulated or generated training data for machine-learning detection.
Correlations between variables can be unrealistic in simulated or generated training data for machine-learning detection.
Generative models, including GAN, diffusion and world models, can produce plausible but physically wrong scenes.
facts.quote: Generative models (GAN, diffusion, world models) produce plausible but physically wrong scenes.

facts.text: Machine-learning detection validation is contaminated when the same generator or assets are used for both training and testing.
facts.quote: Validation is contaminated when the same generator or assets are used for both training and testing.

facts.text: Camera photorealism alone is insufficient for validating simulated or generated data for machine-learning detection.
Radar, lidar and ultrasonic simulation each need modality-appropriate physical correlation.
facts.quote: radar, lidar and ultrasonic simulation each need modality-appropriate physical correlation.
